item.content:encoded:
But what does it do?
I see versions of that question being asked for years, so here's the answer.

+ Spoilers
- Hide

When you use the scissors to cut someone out of a photograph, that person ceases to exist. They are also erased from all records and everyone's memory. You can figure out someone was erased by the gaps left behind.
The description is redacted because the Foundation bosses are worried about someone abusing the thing for personal revenge. Again.

item.content:encoded:
To belatedly answer you and Bryx, I wasn't sure about that too, but it's justified in order to tell its story in a way to develop it. Maybe you could guess at it, but because you don't know what it does up until the end of the addena, it lets you get into these characters and their personal lives. It also opens up several questions that outright stating the effects of wouldn't otherwise do:

+ Spoilers.
- Spoilers.
  1. Is Subject A Professor AW? Presumably yes, but then did he develop these scissors himself?
  2. Do the scissors wholesale erase people, or just their identity and existance? Does it affect the people being erased themselves (IE, are they no longer aware of themselves)?
  3. Regardless of the above answers, how and why do the people remember the person after using the scissors?
- Spoilers.

Aside from the second addendum (which helps solidify the cover-up of information, but actually has no useful purpose for the flow of the article otherwise), I am a huge fan of this. I wasn't sure about it once I got past the first paragraph of the description, but it paid off hugely with the way it told its story. This is one of the few cases where doing such a thing actually pays off, and given how even the final addendum makes sense (and further underscores the horror of this thing), I enjoy it immensely. Easy upvote.

I know this is a bit of a necropost, but another possibility:

Jim in resource allocation found it odd that such a low, 3 digit number had never been allocated, and odder still that there was a large chamber pre-assigned for the eventual SCP. With the caution due his job, he spent several weeks confirming that this wasn't a secret SCP, even CCing the O5s. Eventually he went to catalog the details of the chamber. The last thing he saw was the door sliding open.

It didn't say that the person is necessarily destroyed, just the perception and memory of others…

Alternatively,

The image of SCP-682 became animate and moved its "body" into the path of the scissors, preventing SCP-733 from continuing to cut through the photograph. As nifty as this is, there's nothing in the article to make it an SCP object. I suggest a summary of this be added to the log of anomalous items, this piece itself redesignated a Foundation tale, and the article be rewritten to highlight the real SCP object it's trying so hard to "hint" at; that is, the "unknown tool" used to remove the people from the images.

Downvoted, because articles are for SCP objects. Stories go in the tales section, and if you must blur the line, it's best to err toward the proper section. As a Tale, this would be pretty good.
